answer: Clones share hardware, so they share a rhythm. Each epoch the network fires simultaneous probes at random identity pairs; a falcon-quick reply that lands within milliseconds of its twin's, with the same latency ripple across 20 probes (correlation above 0.9), merges both into one voting seat. Assumed: 1,000 clones on 5 hosts collapse to 5 seats, while an oasis of agents on distinct machines keeps full weight. Limit: shared cloud hosts can cause false merges, so merged agents may appeal.
